caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the 81_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

This is static build/package evidence only. ARM64 is build-identity-bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. ARMHF's maximum GLIBCXX_3.4.21 is within the observed Miyoo Mini fallback provider ceiling GLIBCXX_3.4.24, so both the Mini and A30 profiles clear the ABI screen. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every execution profile and device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced the package, resolver metadata, and both ABI artifacts byte for byte. Their raw logs differ only because parallel Make scheduled the exact reviewed warning/note streams differently; each log independently passes the strict per-owner diagnostic-stream NFA, so reproducibility is semantic at the log layer rather than a false byte-for-byte scheduling claim. The earlier actions-sim-build-core-81-v1 records are excluded and unpromotable because their synthetic path and zero-diagnostic oracle was wrong even though both compilers linked successfully.

The pristine source is commit fa7094910d040baa5fd8b11dbf6a1a618330ecd9, tree d73d124d16714e946ba9490627a4fc38c2aea37a, with no submodules. Upstream Make generates src/version.c from etc/version.c.templ using the full pinned commit; the pipeline verifies generated SHA-256 5a07d38a3bcd84ee5fa9abbdbe0bd706288d8ec4ee8095485447e35dc28a2862 after the build and never injects GIT_VERSION or patches the source. The proof binds 16 C and 12 C++ compiles, exact ABI-specific invocations, the generated-source compile position, and the ordered C++ link through build/link.T.

ARM64 emits exactly 39 reviewed warnings and 6 notes; ARMHF emits exactly 38 reviewed warnings and 11 notes. The contract preserves every literal per-source stream and permits only interleavings that retain each stream's order between its owning compile and the final link. Possible-uninitialized, pointer conversion/truncation, format, and related legacy-code diagnostics remain runtime and maintenance risks; promotion does not assert that they are harmless.

Resolver metadata reports GPLv3, display version 1.0a, p|tzx|t81 content, software rendering, serialized states, libretro_saves=false, and supports_no_game=false. The copied .info text contains unescaped inner quotes in its p/tzx description; current metadata validation proves only exact nonempty bytes and hash identity, not frontend parsing or presentation. Content loading, keyboard and controller input, tape handling, audio/video pacing, reset, save-state round trips, frontend integration, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates.

The selected binaries contain the compiled zx81 and dkchr ROM headers. The source tree is GPLv3, but any public redistribution of those bundled ROM bytes requires a separate human licensing and policy review. Both E2Es fetched the exact source over the network; no offline source bundle or network-disabled rebuild is proven. The portable toolchain archives and loaded image identities are locked, while cached images retain dockerfile_linkage=unverified-local-cache as an explicit provenance limitation.

The rebuilt ARM64 dependency set drops the shipped baseline's libgcc_s and libm requirements and records the AArch64 loader that the imported report omitted, while the rebuilt ARMHF artifact adds libgcc_s, libm, GLIBCXX_3.4.20, and CXXABI_1.3.9 relative to the shipped baseline. ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float requiring GLIBC_2.4; provider compatibility is therefore unverified. The software-only artifacts bind only to ra64-universal-v1 and ra32-a30-v1 and provide no basis for device-specific duplicate builds; every device view remains ineligible pending provider and target-runtime evidence.
